sources.note: Nothing. The article reviews the classification debate and compiles Hervey's two wordlists (307 items, Kena. I / Kena. II / Kena. Stev.) from Blagden 1906 as an appendix; there is no phonology section and no mention of stress, accent or tone. The transcribed forms carry vowel diacritics but no stress marks.

sources.citation: Skeat, W. W. & C. O. Blagden. 1906. Pagan Races of the Malay Peninsula, vol. 2. London: Macmillan. (Kenaboi subdivision pp. 403-405; Comparative Vocabulary appendix, 'Accent' p. 773)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing Kenaboi-specific. p. 405: for Kenaboi 'no grammatical information whatever is available'. p. 773 ('Accent'), a blanket remark across all the Peninsula aboriginal wordlists: 'The data with regard to accent and emphasis are very meagre.. As a rule, the accent in all the aboriginal dialects appears to fall on the final syllable. This is most marked, however, in Sakai.. but the tendency is also traceable in Jakun, even in words of Malayan affinity.'
